extracted.intended_audience: BlackRock clients, investors, portfolio companies, and other stewardship stakeholders (institutional and retail clients)
extracted.subtask_description: BlackRock’s corporate statement of principles and operational criteria for conducting investment stewardship (engagement, proxy voting, industry dialogue and reporting) on behalf of clients across index and active strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stewardship as fiduciary to clients
rubrics_metrics.description: Investment stewardship is core to BlackRock’s role as an asset manager and a fiduciary to our clients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stewardship activities are performed to serve clients’ interests and objectives; decisions, engagement and voting are undertaken as part of fiduciary duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose — support durable, risk-adjusted financial returns
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage with companies and vote at shareholder meetings to encourage sound corporate governance and business practices that support companies in delivering durable, risk-adjusted financial returns over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stewardship actions should be oriented toward outcomes that protect and enhance long-term, risk-adjusted returns for clients, not toward other objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive, ongoing engagement to deepen understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Build strong relationships through constructive, ongoing dialogue with boards and executive management to deepen our understanding of a company’s business model and how they are overseeing material business risks and opportunities over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engagement is used to inform voting and stewardship decisions; emphasis on relationship-building and learning about oversight of material risks/opportunities rather than adversarial or one-off contacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make decisions consistent with clients’ stated objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Stewardship decisions (engagement, voting, program application) are focused on being consistent with clients’ stated objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BlackRock offers different stewardship/policy options so that the approach taken aligns with each client’s expressed investment preferences and goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four stewardship program pillars
rubrics_metrics.description: BlackRock’s stewardship program is structured around four key pillars: (1) engaging with boards and management; (2) voting at shareholder meetings; (3) contributing to industry dialogue on stewardship; (4) reporting on activities to inform clients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each pillar represents a discrete area of stewardship activity and expectation: engagement informs voting; voting acts on behalf of clients who authorize BlackRock; industry dialogue shares perspectives; reporting keeps clients informed via publications and direct communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voting on behalf of clients who authorize BlackRock
rubrics_metrics.description: Vote at shareholder meetings on management and shareholder proposals for clients who have authorized BlackRock to vote on their behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voting activity is conditional on client authorization; voting decisions are informed by engagement and the firm’s stewardship policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribute to industry dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: Contribute to industry dialogue on stewardship to share BlackRock’s perspectives on matters that may impact clients’ investments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public advocacy, participation in consultations and industry forums are used to influence norms and practices that affect investee companies and clients’ investments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report stewardship activities to clients
rubrics_metrics.description: Report on stewardship activities to inform clients about BlackRock’s stewardship efforts on their behalf through a range of publications on the website and direct client communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparent reporting is expected as part of the stewardship program; multiple channels (publications, client communications) are used to keep clients informed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer stewardship choice options to clients
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a range of stewardship options to reflect clients’ individual investment choices and goals through a selection of proxy voting policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clients can select among available stewardship/policy options so that the stewardship applied to their holdings matches their preferences; BlackRock is committed to providing choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: BlackRock Voting Choice (pass-through voting) option
rubrics_metrics.description: BlackRock Voting Choice — sometimes known as pass-through voting — provides eligible clients with more opportunities to participate in the proxy voting process, where legally and operationally viable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pass-through voting is available only to eligible clients and only in jurisdictions and circumstances where it is legally and operationally feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Climate and decarbonization stewardship program eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The climate and decarbonization stewardship program applies only to funds that have climate and decarbonization objectives and that have been explicitly approved for inclusion in the program by the respective governing body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separately managed account clients may instruct BlackRock to apply the program to their holdings; BIS and BAIS administer the program separately for strategies in their scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate administration by BIS and BAIS; roles and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: BlackRock’s stewardship policies are developed and implemented separately by two independent teams, BlackRock Investment Stewardship (BIS) and BlackRock Active Investment Stewardship (BAIS). BIS handles stewardship for index equity strategies; BAIS partners with active investment teams for their holdings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teams operate independently and administer programs for the strategies in their remit; BIS is a dedicated function for index equities (representing a large share of public equity AUM), while BAIS works with active teams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounding in widely recognized corporate governance norms
rubrics_metrics.description: Both stewardship teams’ general approach is grounded in widely recognized norms of corporate governance and shareholder rights and responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stewardship actions and policies reflect established governance norms and expectations about shareholder rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory compliance and non-interference with control
rubrics_metrics.description: BlackRock complies fully with regulatory requirements (e.g., SEC guidance on Schedule 13G) and does not engage with portfolio companies for the purpose, or with the effect, of changing or influencing control of any company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engagement activities are conducted within applicable regulatory constraints and are explicitly not intended to change company control; adherence to disclosure/ownership reporting rules is maintained.
